title: Tenali Raman and the Deaf Horse

full_text:
An arrogant courtier named Somadeva was desperate to impress King Krishnadevaraya with his supposed 'esoteric intuition'. Whenever the King spoke of military maneuvers, Somadeva would nod knowingly and whisper:
'Yes, Maharaj! I sensed that through my mystical intuition! I can hear what common ears cannot!'

Tenali Raman decided to cure the courtier of his pretentious clairvoyance.

King Krishnadevaraya had recently purchased an old cavalry horse that had gone completely, stone-deaf due to cannon fire in an ancient border siege.
Tenali brought the deaf horse to the palace courtyard where Somadeva was boasting to other courtiers.

Tenali whispered to Somadeva with an air of urgent mystery:
'Friend Somadeva, this is no ordinary cavalry horse. It is a sacred "Oracle Steed" from the Himalayas!
When you hold your ear close to its mouth, it whispers secret prophecies about the future of the empire!
I listened just now, and it spoke of great glory. But only a man of profound esoteric intuition like you can understand its deeper cosmic messages!'

Somadeva’s vanity was instantly ignited:
'Of course, Tenali! My ears are attuned to the cosmic frequencies!'

Somadeva walked up to the old horse, bowed with great ceremony, and leaned his right ear directly against the horse’s lips.
The horse, which was stone-deaf and had no idea what was happening, simply chewed its oats contentedly.

After three minutes of theatrical listening, Somadeva stood up, his face filled with profound, spiritual awe:
'Ah! Transcendent wisdom! The sacred steed spoke to me in ancient celestial Sanskrit!
It whispered: "The Emperor’s fame shall conquer the three worlds, and Somadeva shall be appointed Chief Counselor of State!"'

Tenali Raman burst into body-shaking, roaring laughter!
King Krishnadevaraya and the courtiers, who had been watching from the balcony, broke into deafening applause and laughter!

The King came down the stairs, laughing so hard he wiped tears from his eyes:
'Somadeva! Thou hast heard celestial Sanskrit from a horse that has been completely, stone-deaf for eight years!'

Tenali clapped the courtier on the shoulder:
'A deaf horse speaks nothing, but a vain fool hears whatever flattery pleases his pride!'

Somadeva turned bright purple, shrank with humiliation, and fled the courtyard.
He never again claimed to possess 'esoteric intuition', while Tenali showed that pretentious vanity makes a man hear voices in empty air.
moral: Pretending to hear secrets to appear wise leads to comedic humiliation; honest listening is the foundation of truth.
